probe/freeze: Does the residual stream at some layer know whether a word is a noun? Freeze the model, and collect its stream, h, for many words, each labeled noun or not.
probe/fit: Then fit a linear classifier on them: a score, w dot h plus b, positive for a noun. Only w and b are trained. The model never changes.
probe/example: Say h is two, minus one and a half, w is one, two and minus two, and b is a half. The score is two, minus two, minus one, plus a half: minus a half. The probe says: not a noun.
test/held: Now test the probe on words it was not fit on. A score above zero predicts noun.
test/count: It matches the true label on six of eight: an accuracy of zero point seven five, where a coin flip would get zero point five.
meaning/there: High accuracy shows the information is in the stream, written so that one linear map can read it.
meaning/use: It does not show that the model uses it. Present is not the same as used, and testing use takes an experiment on the model itself.
meaning/linear: And the probe is kept linear on purpose. A large network could work out the answer by itself, and then its success would describe the probe, not the stream.
